today_items.agenda:
Do this AFTER the guidelines check on Thursday.

USE THE OFFICIAL TEMPLATE - do not build one from scratch:
  web.mit.edu/thesis/tex/  -> official MIT thesis template in LaTeX, on Overleaf.

SET UP IN THIS ORDER:

  2. Fill title page fields: name, previous degrees (BS Systems Engineering, West Point), BOTH degrees to be awarded, conferral date (February or June - matches the degree-list decision on 29 Sep), supervisor(s), department/program.
  3. Use the DUAL DEGREE sample title page as reference - extra committee members.
  4. Skeleton chapters matching the milestone plan: intro, literature review, methods, results, conclusion.
  5. Turn on Overleaf's Git or GitHub integration so the document is version-controlled from day one, not a single blob that can be lost.
  6. Share with Afreen Siddiqi and Dr. Palladino for read access now - not the week you want feedback.

An empty but correctly formatted document with real chapter headings is what makes 'work on thesis' become 'write section 2.1'. That is the whole point of doing it in September.

overdue_items.name: TSK Thesis guidelines check: TPP + Institute-wide (before Overleaf)
overdue_items.agenda:
Read the rules BEFORE creating the document, so the Overleaf file is right from the first commit rather than reformatted in January.

TWO LAYERS, and they are different documents:

1. INSTITUTE-WIDE (MIT Libraries, binding on everyone)
   libraries.mit.edu/distinctive-collections/thesis-specs/
   Key points already confirmed:
     - Title page is ALWAYS page 1; every page counted in one consecutive sequence including prefatory material, figures, appendices.
     - Abstract: 500 words or less, single-spaced, immediately after the title page. Avoid formulas/special characters.
     - Body may be single, 1.5, or double spaced. Abstract, biography, notes, bibliography, acknowledgements are single-spaced.
     - NO signature page in the final document - but your DEPARTMENT may require a separate one.
     - Sans serif font suggested (not required) for readability.
     - Degree conferral date must read February, May/June, or September only.
     - Title page and abstract must MATCH the metadata you submit to the Libraries exactly.
   Spec was revised April 2026 - read the current version, not a cached PDF.

2. DEPARTMENT (TPP and AeroAstro - you are dual, so check BOTH)
   Ask each program office directly. Departments set their own committee composition, signature page, internal deadlines, and page/chapter conventions, and the Institute page does not cover these.
   For a DUAL degree the Libraries publish a specific sample title page: 'Dual degree with extra committee members'. Use that one, not the standard example.

QUESTIONS TO GET ANSWERED IN WRITING:
  - Does TPP have its own thesis format guide or internal deadline earlier than 12 Dec?
  - For the dual degree, do BOTH departments sign, and how many readers total?
  - Does either department require a separate signature page?
  - Is there a TPP-specific abstract or policy-content requirement?

Contacts: mit-theses@mit.edu for Institute questions. Barb / Rachael for TPP. AeroAstro grad office for 16.
